hook.text: Two friends lose each other at a festival. No phones. Where do they go to meet? Both must guess the same spot.

buildup.text: Coordination games have multiple equilibria. The challenge isn't incentives—it's picking the same option.

discovery.text: Thomas Schelling found people use 'focal points'—obvious choices that stand out. Most pick noon at the clock.

twist.text: Focal points are cultural. Americans meet at Grand Central; the Japanese pick Hachiko. Context creates consensus.

climax.text: Driving on the left or right is a coordination game: the side doesn't matter, but everyone must agree.

punchline.text: Sometimes the only problem is picking.

quiz.question: What is a focal point in coordination games?
options: An obvious choice that people gravitate toward
